subject: English
central_question: How can open communication and respect for tradition allow personal artistic choice and cultural innovation to coexist?
in_scope_units: Reflect and Respond on musical instruments, preferences and figurative phrases
Act I: Shruti, her fusion group and her fear of telling Nabin about the concert
Act II: the family confrontation over Indo-Western fusion music and Shrutis apology for hiding the practice
Act III: Nabin and Leela attend the rehearsal, Nabin reconsiders his position and the family conflict is resolved
Critical Reflection on generational difference, duty, passion, cultural diversity and the plays ending
Vocabulary and Structures in Context: aside, non-lexical fillers, music vocabulary, exclamatory sentences and reported speech
Listening about the yazh, stress and intonation, script writing and Learning Beyond the Text on stage directions, recycled and indigenous instruments
Reading for Appreciation: A Friend Found in Music and the poem Music with metaphor, mood and phrasal verbs
banned_topics: Technical music theory beyond the ragas, aalaaps, instruments and terms stated in the source
Biographical information about musicians or playwright Mitra Phukan beyond the supplied text

known_pitfalls.claim: Shruti rejects Hindustani classical music and her fathers tradition.
known_pitfalls.correction: She says she respects her fathers opinions and classical training but also wants to try fusion music.

known_pitfalls.claim: Nabin changes his mind because Shruti defeats him in an argument.
known_pitfalls.correction: He changes after hearing the rehearsal and after Leela reminds him of his own earlier conflict with family tradition over choosing the violin.

known_pitfalls.claim: The play presents tradition and innovation as mutually exclusive.
known_pitfalls.correction: The ending shows Shruti maintaining the notes of the raga within fusion and Nabin offering the group his music room.

known_pitfalls.claim: An aside is ordinary dialogue heard by every character.
known_pitfalls.correction: The language section defines aside as a theatrical device in which a character communicates to the audience while other characters are treated as unaware.

recommended_example_progression: Check Your Understanding after Act I: explain Shrutis dilemma
Act II summary: identify the clash between traditional and contemporary musical preferences
Critical Reflection: assess Nabin as both strict parent and artist shaped by his own past
Vocabulary and Structures in Context: identify an aside and convert exclamatory speech to reported speech
A Friend Found in Music: explain the metaphors used for music as comfort and therapy
ncert_end_of_chapter_exercises_reference: Each act is followed by Check Your Understanding, then the play has Critical Reflection, language, listening, speaking and script-writing tasks; the later music poem has appreciation, reflection and vocabulary activities.
